title: Progressive Release Mesh: policy-driven deployment orchestration across Hosted / Dedicated / Private
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Goal: Implement a unified 'release mesh' that lets teams declare progressive-release policies (canary percentages, A/B splits, shadow taps, automated rollback rules) as a single policy document that the control plane can translate into environment-specific execution for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Background: We need parity in developer-facing configuration (one policy DSL) but the runtime constraints differ: hosted can manipulate traffic via internal routing and multi-tenant pools, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation, Private may have no sidecar or centralized router and enforces strict network and upgrade windows. Historically we've duplicated rollout logic across controllers resulting in drift and gaps in safety behavior for Private customers.

Scope:
- Create a policy DSL for progressive releases covering: percentage-based canaries, time-based promotion windows, A/B experiment variants, shadow duplication rules, metric-based auto-rollback predicates, and environment affinity (route to region/tier).
- Implement a translation layer that converts DSL into environment-specific plans: e.g., Hosted -> gateway routing + runtime canary, Dedicated -> capacity-aware ring-based pointer updates, Private -> instructions for customer-side load balancer + agent-driven gradual weight updates.
- Safety and audit: ensure audit logs, immutable policy hashes per rollout, and enforce maximum allowed canary percent/configs in Private via admin override in policy translation.
- Auto-rollback engine that subscribes to metric streams (latency, error-rate, model-quality signals) and executes rollback plans; for Private, produce operator actions and an opt-in agent channel to perform automatic rollbacks when permitted.

Non-goals: full rollout UI; deep UX polish for console (we'll add console hooks in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Single policy DSL documented in design doc and supported by schema (json-schema) and examples for text-generation and embeddings models.
Translation layer prototypes route the same policy to mock Hosted/Dedicated/Private executors and produce executable plans with no dropped config fields.
End-to-end smoke demonstrating: a 5% canary in Hosted, a 10% ring update in Dedicated, and an operator-guided 5% incremental rollout for Private using the same policy file.

Auto-rollback rule triggers on a simulated latency spike and reverts to previous model version in Hosted and Dedicated; Private produces actionable operator command and audit entry when auto-rollback is disallowed by customer policy.
Auditability: every generated plan has a policy hash and is logged to the audit stream with linking metadata (policy key, rollout id, env).
design_notes: DSL shape: keep small core (traffic, variants, triggers, safety_limits) + extensible 'annotations' for environment hints.
Translation approach: layered adapters - CorePolicy -> EnvPlan -> Executor. Adapters live in control plane; Private adapter emits 'operator actions' and optional signed webhook to on-prem agent.
Metrics for rollback: primary SLOs (p95 latency, 5xx rate) + model-quality delta from canary evaluation hooks (we'll use existing eval service to feed a quality score stream).
Safety defaults: max_canary_percent=20, min_observation_window=2m, require_manual_for_db-schema-changes annotated at policy level.
Compatibility: reuse existing rollout IDs and tracing tags so Console and observability can correlate traces across environments.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize DSL schema and write transform tests (Marco + SRE).
Week 2: implement Hosted adapter and basic executor integration using gateway routing primitives.
Week 3: Dedicated adapter: integrate with capacity manager to translate percentages into node/slot allocations; smoke on staging Dedicated cluster.
Week 4: Private adapter: define operator action format, signable manifests, and opt-in agent protocol; test with customer VM in lab.
Week 5: Auto-rollback engine: wire metric ingestion, implement predicate evaluation, and test with canary workflows.
Week 6: End-to-end demos, docs, and handoff to Console/Docs/Support.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Private customers may reject automated agent actions for security reasons. Mitigation: default to 'operator-action' outputs and require explicit opt-in and signed manifests; provide an easy 'accept and execute' CLI for operators.
Risk: Metric noise causing flapping rollbacks. Mitigation: require multi-window confirmation and configurable debounce thresholds; tie into existing anomaly-detect service for smoothing.
Risk: Resource fragmentation in Dedicated if naive percentage->slot translation. Mitigation: consult capacity manager and provide backpressure/queuing suggestions in plan; expose 'max-burst' control.
Risk: DSL complexity leading to user errors. Mitigation: ship a validator and example library; include 'lint' tool in SDK.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL schema and translator edge-cases.
Integration test harness that spins up mock Hosted / Dedicated / Private executors and verifies behavioral parity.
Chaos test: inject latency and error spikes during canary windows to ensure rollback triggers and audit logs are emitted.
Security review checklist: ensure signed manifests for Private adapter, no secrets transmitted, RBAC gating for auto-rollback toggles.
